title: Why This Octopus Carries a Coconut Across the Seafloor
subject: coconut octopus

scenes.text: An octopus drags a coconut across the seafloor. Why?
It's the veined octopus, also called the coconut octopus, off Indonesia.
It finds discarded coconut shell halves, scoops them up, and walks away, up to twenty meters.
It tucks the shell under its body and tiptoes on two arms, like a stilt walker.
Why bother? The sandy bottom has nowhere to hide, so it brings its own hideout.
When danger shows up, it stacks two halves into a sphere and hides inside. That's why it hauls a coconut.

description:
An octopus drags a coconut across the seafloor, and it has a very good reason.
The veined octopus carries shell halves up to twenty meters, then hides inside them when danger shows up.
What would you carry around for protection?
first_comment: Scientists called this the first invertebrate seen using tools to prepare for danger. What other animal would you nominate?
